'''Valentine Joseph''' (27 January 1929 – 15 March 2017) was a [[Sri Lankan Tamils|Sri Lankan Tamil]] mathematician, noted for his contributions to education.<ref name="CP170317"/><ref name="ST300417"/><ref name="UCAANSW"/>

==Early life and education==
Joseph was born in [[Penang]], [[British Malaya|Malaya]] to [[Sri Lankan Tamils|Sri Lankan Tamil]] parents. His extended family were [[Roman Catholics]], with his cousin, [[Dominic Vendargon]], becoming the first [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Kuala Lumpur|Archbishop of Kuala Lumpur]]. Joseph commenced school at [[St. Xavier's Institution]] in Penang in 1935.<ref name="ST300417">{{cite news|last1=Codippily|first1=Hilarian|title=Professor Valentine Joseph: Scholar and teacher par excellence|url=http://www.sundaytimes.lk/170430/plus/238249-238249.html|access-date=28 August 2017|work=[[The Sunday Times (Sri Lanka)|The Sunday Times]]|date=30 April 2017|location=Colombo, Sri Lanka}}</ref>

Joseph prepared for the [[University Entrance Examination]] as a science student studying pure mathematics, applied mathematics, physics and geography at [[St. Patrick's College, Jaffna]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2017}} In 1949, Joseph entered [[University of Ceylon]] (Colombo campus) to study for a four-year mathematics degree, obtaining a [[first class degree]] in three years.<ref name="ST300417"/>

==Career==
Joseph joined the University of Ceylon (Colombo campus) as an assistant lecturer in 1952 where he stayed for the next 42 years.<ref name="ST300417"/> As one of the prominent mathematicians in [[Sri Lanka]] at the time, he represented the country at many international gatherings and organisations such as the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in Trieste, Italy.<ref name="CP170317">{{cite news|title=Admired University of Colombo Professor Valentine Joseph passes away|url=http://www.colombopage.com/archive_17A/Mar17_1489708170CH.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170317021928/http://www.colombopage.com/archive_17A/Mar17_1489708170CH.php|url-status=usurped|archive-date=17 March 2017|access-date=28 August 2017|work=Colombo Page|date=17 March 2017|location=Indianapolis, U.S.A.}}</ref><ref name="ST300417"/> He was sent by the university to [[King's College London]] in 1956 to commence a doctoral thesis in [[mathematical physics]], joining a renowned group of General Relativity specialists, under the guidance of Professor [[Felix Pirani]], to work on developing Einstein's [[Theory of general relativity|Theory of General Relativity]].<ref name="ST300417"/><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_99CygAACAAJ|title=Mechanics and Optics in General Relativity|last=Joseph|first=Valentine|publisher=King's College London. Department of Mathematics|year=1967|location=London}}</ref> Joseph went on to publish a number of academic papers pertaining to this subject.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Joseph|first=Valentine|date=1958|title=On Apparent Luminosity In General Relativity|url=https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/118/6/631/2602249/On-Apparent-Luminosity-in-General-Relativity|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume=118|issue=6|pages=631–639|bibcode=1958MNRAS.118..631J|doi=10.1093/mnras/118.6.631|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Joseph|first=Valentine|date=1957|title=Physical Properties of Some Empty Space-Times|journal=Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society|volume=53|issue=4|pages=836–842|bibcode=1957PCPS...53..836J|doi=10.1017/S0305004100032953|s2cid=122817687 }}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Joseph|first=Valentine|date=1966|title=A spatially homogeneous gravitational field|journal=Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society|volume=62|issue=1|pages=87–89|bibcode=1966PCPS...62...87J|doi=10.1017/S030500410003958X|s2cid=120271953 }}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last=Lorenz-Petzold, Joseph|date=1985|title=Comment on the Bianchi Type-V Vacuum Model|journal=General Relativity and Gravitation|volume=17|issue=5|pages=509–513|doi=10.1007/BF00761908|bibcode=1985GReGr..17..509L|s2cid=58925615}}</ref>

His output of articles and lectures covering these themes, spanned a period of over 60 years, from 1955 to 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sayakkara|first1=Asanka P.|title=Prof. Valentine Joseph|url=http://recolog.blogspot.co.uk/2016/05/prof-valentine-joseph.html|publisher=fetch( ); decode( ); execute( ); // the cycle of my life...|access-date=28 August 2017|date=13 May 2016}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=September 2017}}

During his university career, which spanned over four decades, Joseph taught several generations of students, first as a lecturer and later as a professor.<ref name="ST300417"/><ref>{{cite news|last1=Warusawithana|first1=Srima|title=Universities then and now|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=70696|access-date=28 August 2017|work=[[The Island (Sri Lanka)|The Island]]|date=20 January 2013|location=Colombo, Sri Lanka}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Former professor Valentine Joseph has passed away|url=http://science.cmb.ac.lk/former-professor-valentine-joseph-has-passed-away/|publisher=[[Faculty of Science, University of Colombo]]|access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Prof Valentine Joseph passed away on March 15, 2017|url=http://www.cufsaa.com/2017/03/prof-valentine-joseph/|publisher=Colombo University Faculty of Science Alumni Association of North America|access-date=28 August 2017|date=19 March 2017|location=Edison, New Jersey, U.S.A.}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=September 2017}} In addition to his university duties, Joseph was Chief Examiner for the GCE Advanced level examinations in mathematics for over twenty years, setting exam questions which were regarded to have been creative.<ref name="TI290317">{{cite news|last1=Premadasa|first1=Kirthi|title=A tribute to a most beautiful mind|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=162698|access-date=28 August 2017|work=[[The Island (Sri Lanka)|The Island]]|date=29 March 2017|location=Colombo, Sri Lanka}}</ref> He also authored an A-level mathematics textbook in [[Sinhalese language|Sinhala]] entitled Gathikaya in 1994.<ref name="ST300417"/><ref>{{Cite book|title=Gathikaya|last=Joseph|first=Valentine|publisher=Educational Publications Department|year=1994|location=Colombo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Do we need to look at Singapore math? Why not relay on our own resources?|url=https://sites.google.com/site/teachersarojiswebsite/education-in-sri-lanka/math-education-in-sri-lanka/do-we-need-to-look-at-singapore-math-why-not-relay-on-our-own-resources|publisher=Teacher Saroji's Website|access-date=28 August 2017}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=September 2017}} He maintained an interest in teaching throughout his later retirement, and in 2016 published an updated English edition of his book, ''Dynamics: Newtonian Relativity''.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Miriyagalla|first1=Das|title=The Era of Prof. Valentine Joseph|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=162312|access-date=28 August 2017|work=[[The Island (Sri Lanka)|The Island]]|date=22 March 2017|location=Colombo, Sri Lanka}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Dynamics: Newtonian Relativity|last=Joseph|first=V.|publisher=Educational Publications Department|year=2016|location=No. 107D, Havelock Road, Colombo 05}}</ref>

Joseph gave his final lecture in 2016 entitled "Einstein: The Wunderkind".<ref name="UCAANSW">{{cite web|title=Professor Valentine Joseph|url=https://cuaansw.org.au/blog/|publisher=University of Colombo Alumni Association NSW Inc.|access-date=28 August 2017|date=2016-10-30}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=September 2017}}

==Personal life==
Joseph married Antonia (née Arulanandam) in 1965 and they had two children, Umesh and Arulesh.<ref name="CP170317"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Obituaries|url=http://dailynews.lk/2017/03/17/obituaries/110698/obituaries|access-date=3 September 2017|work=[[Daily News (Sri Lanka)|Daily News]]|date=17 March 2017|location=Colombo, Sri Lanka}}</ref>

Joseph and his family were badly affected during the [[Black July|ethnic riots of 1983]].<ref name="CP170317" /> According to witnesses, before a mob ransacked his house in [[Colombo]], Joseph was asked whether he was a [[Tamils|Tamil]] or a [[Sinhalese people|Sinhalese]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uthr.org/Book/CHA09.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010923140726/http://www.uthr.org/Book/CHA09.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=23 September 2001|title=Sri Lanka's Black July|website=University Teachers for Human Rights (Jaffna), Sri Lanka|series=9}}</ref> He replied in [[Sinhalese language|Sinhala]]: "I am a human being".{{citation needed|date=August 2017}} Following this statement, he was physically assaulted.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Professor Valentine Joseph Commemorative Issue|journal=CUFSAA Newsletter|date=8 June 2017|volume=2|issue=1}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=September 2017}}
